title: A push to dev runs CI twice for one SHA, and the overlap is what reddened the bound test
description:
Filed from WCLI-53, which deliberately left this open: the test side is now robust to contention, and this is the configuration side.

MEASURED (runs 36565482468 and 36565512667, recorded in WCLI-53). A push to dev fires both the push workflow and the pull_request workflow for one SHA. .github/workflows/ci.yml scopes concurrency per ref — group ward-cli-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }} — and a push to dev has ref refs/heads/dev while the pull request has refs/pull/N/merge, so the two do not share a group and do not cancel each other. The push job ran 12:02:12Z to 12:02:54Z (42 s); the pull_request job on the same SHA ran 12:02:28Z to 12:04:05Z (97 s); they overlapped by 26 s on the same runner group and the contended run took more than twice as long. That contention is what pushed a 150 ms provider bound to 474 ms in the pull_request job while the push job passed on identical bytes.

WHY IT IS FILED RATHER THAN FIXED. WCLI-53 made every wall-clock bound in the suite either deterministic or measured-for-margin, so the suite no longer breaks under this overlap; but the overlap still doubles the work on every push to dev and still puts two jobs on one ephemeral runner concurrently, which is a CI capacity question rather than a test question. The options are not equivalent and none was chosen here: keying concurrency on the SHA so the second run cancels the first, removing the push trigger for dev and relying on the pull_request run, or leaving it as it is because two independent runs on the same bytes is a deliberate signal. Decide which, then change .github/workflows/ci.yml and, if a job is renamed or removed, the ruleset requiring Check, Docs and Tracker integrity in the same change.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The overlap is decided and recorded: one of cancel, remove the dev push trigger, or keep and say why
The decision is executed in .github/workflows/ci.yml, or recorded as a deliberate keep with its reason
If any job name changes, the dev ruleset names it in the same change, so no merge blocks on a check that never reports

plan: 1. Pre-fix control: open a dev-to-main PR (head dev) and read the run list for the dev tip SHA, expecting the duplicate pull_request run; close it.
2. Decide: scope the pull_request trigger to base branch dev, keeping push coverage of dev and main; record why this beats cancel, remove-dev-push, and keep.
3. Implement in .github/workflows/ci.yml; run bun run check, lore check and lore validate --strict locally.
4. Land through a PR into dev; confirm the merge push produces exactly one run for its SHA.
5. Treatment: open the same dev-to-main PR and confirm no run is created; close it.
6. Record both measurements; confirm no job name changes, so the dev ruleset needs no edit.
implementationNotes:
DECIDED 2026-09-29 (AC1): scope the pull_request trigger to base branch dev, so the duplicate run is never created. The second run is redundant by construction - a pull request whose base is main is in this repository always the dev to main promotion, and because main is an ancestor of dev its test merge IS the dev tip, so the push run covers the same bytes.

WHY NOT THE THREE NAMED OPTIONS.
- Cancel: two runs are still created, one is aborted only after a runner pickup, its check runs report cancelled on the SHA, and re-keying the concurrency group on the SHA would lose the per-ref cancellation that currently stops two rapid pushes to dev from running concurrently. It treats the symptom after paying for it.
- Remove the push trigger for dev: dev's own tip would then be untested unless a promotion pull request happened to be open, which makes the gated ref's coverage depend on an unrelated pull request - and the pull_request run tests the merge ref rather than the ref that carries the merge.
- Keep: the second run tests identical bytes. Measured cost of the overlap is in the description and WCLI-53; a deliberate keep needs the second run to carry an independent signal, and it does not.

RECORDED IN THE FILE: the block above the on: key in .github/workflows/ci.yml states the decision, the measurement it rests on and what it means for a promotion pull request, so the next reader gets it without the tracker.

MEASURED, post-fix (AC2), 2026-09-29. The change is de3439b on dev, through opum-ai/ward-cli#116.

- CONTROL, before the change: PR opum-ai/ward-cli#115 (base main, head dev, opened only to measure and closed unmerged) created pull_request run 36592317844 at 15:43:02Z on 8fc98a1, whose push run 36591719507 had completed at 15:39:14Z. The instrument could produce the two-run answer.
- TREATMENT, after the change: PR opum-ai/ward-cli#117 (same shape, opened 15:46:34Z, closed unmerged) created NO run for de3439b in 80 s of polling. Pre-fix, its twin produced one within 10 s. That is the one-SHA-one-run property, measured rather than inferred.
- The merge push itself is the only run for de3439b: run 36592695262, event push. One SHA, one set of jobs.
- A pull request whose base is dev still runs: PR opum-ai/ward-cli#116's own run 36592546690 on 463c264, all three required contexts green, which is also what the merge gate was decided on. The trigger change removes the base-main run, not the base-dev one.

AC3: no job name changed. Parsed from the committed file: Check, Docs, Tracker integrity - the same three contexts the dev ruleset requires (ruleset 24097150, each pinned to integration 15368), re-read rather than assumed.

FINDING, filed separately and outside this task: run 36592695262 failed on the vault-store test that corrupts a ciphertext on disk and requires the read to fail closed - Expected vault_authentication_failed, Received not-a-ward-error - on a tree byte-identical to 463c264, whose run passed all three contexts. Two facts make it independent of this change: the trees are identical (611b296d both), and this run had the runner group to itself, so the duplication this task removed is not its cause. A re-run of the failed job is in flight; the finding is filed as its own task with the CI evidence.

CLOSE DEFERRED, deliberately: the last evidence for this task can only exist after it lands, so the closing record rides with this repository's next pull request rather than travelling alone (opum-sdlc, deliver). The task stays In Progress until that lands.
finalSummary:
Delivered in opum-ai/ward-cli#116: the pull_request trigger in .github/workflows/ci.yml is scoped to base branch dev, so one SHA runs one set of jobs.

Decision, recorded on the task and in the comment above the on: key. The duplicate was the dev-to-main promotion pull request: its test merge IS the dev tip, because main is always an ancestor of dev, so the push run already covered the same bytes. Cancelling was rejected (two runs are still created, one is aborted only after a runner pickup, and re-keying the concurrency group on the SHA would lose the per-ref cancellation that stops two rapid pushes to dev racing), and so was removing the dev push trigger (dev's tip would then be untested unless a promotion pull request happened to be open, and the pull_request run tests a merge ref rather than the ref).

Evidence. Before the change, measured live rather than inferred: opum-ai/ward-cli#115 (base main, head dev, opened only to measure, closed unmerged) created pull_request run 36592317844 at 15:43:02Z on 8fc98a1, a SHA whose push run 36591719507 had already completed at 15:39:14Z. After it, the same shape - opum-ai/ward-cli#117, also closed unmerged - created no run at all for de3439b in 80 s. The merge gate was run 36592546690 covering 463c264, all three required contexts green, and the landed commit de3439b carries exactly one run, 36592695262 (push). No job name changed, so the dev ruleset needed no edit; it was re-read rather than assumed (ruleset 24097150, Check/Docs/Tracker integrity pinned to integration 15368, main still carries no rules).

The Check job on that landing run went red on a tree byte-identical to the passing one and green on an unchanged re-run. It is not this task's cause - the run had the runner group to itself - and it is filed as WCLI-59 with the reproduction.
